kurzfassung: Victoria Aveyard shares her unexpected journey from studying screenwriting at USC to publishing bestselling fantasy series like Red Queen. She discusses how her cinematic training and early experiences with fan fiction shaped her fast-paced storytelling style. Additionally, she offers insights into her transition to adult fantasy with her new duology starter, Tempest.
stichpunkte: Fan fiction provided an early, anonymous environment for receiving feedback and discovering strengths as a writer.
Studying screenwriting at the USC School of Cinematography instilled a deep understanding of structure, plot, and character arcs.
The initial concept for Red Queen sparked from an image of a girl in an arena defeating her executioner with lightning.
Victoria wrote the first draft of Red Queen in six months at her parents' coffee table after college.
A manager passed her unedited first draft to a New York literary agency, leading to a book deal within two weeks of submission.
Social media engagement has evolved from chasing viral videos to building deeper connections with an established readership.
Tempest is set against the fall of the Golden Age of Piracy and follows a former noblewoman forced to hunt down a pirate captain.
Young adult fiction focuses on discovering identity, whereas adult fiction explores characters who already know who they are.
Scrivener serves as the primary software tool for organizing complex fantasy world-building and multiple point-of-view chapters.

clips.hook: Discovering screenwriting through George Lucas and USC film school.
clips.text: A televised tribute to George Lucas revealed the existence of college programs dedicated to cinematic storytelling, inspiring a shift toward film school.

clips.hook: Selling a debut novel just before college loans came due.
clips.text: Securing a book deal happened rapidly right on the deadline of financial obligations, launching a more than decade-long publishing career.

clips.hook: The secret behind fast-paced storytelling in young adult fiction.
clips.text: The high narrative velocity found in young adult books stems directly from the tight pacing principles taught in screenwriting.

clips.hook: Choosing J.R.R. Tolkien for a rainy dinner in Paris.
clips.text: If given the chance, the fantasy pioneer would be invited to a Parisian bistro to discuss the mechanics of building an epic world from constructed languages.

beschreibung:
#1 New York Times bestselling author Victoria Aveyard spoke with us about her journey from USC screenwriting to publishing, her writing process, and her upcoming adult fantasy debut, TEMPEST.

Victoria Aveyard is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of the RED QUEEN series and the REALM BREAKER trilogy. Her books have sold over eight million copies and been published in more than 40 languages.

Her highly anticipated adult fantasy debut, Tempest, is the first book in The Lyrian Sea duology. Set against the fall of the Golden Age of Piracy, the book follows a former noblewoman facing execution for treason unless she helps the Empire hunt down its greatest enemy.

#1 New York Times bestselling author Rebecca Yarros said of the book, “Victoria Aveyard's first foray into adult fantasy is a triumphant, epic adventure on the high seas. What an exciting, captivating read to spend your weekend with!”

In this file Victoria Aveyard, Milena, and I discussed:

Her deliberate pivot in both creative growth and reader demand

How she sold her debut novel within two weeks of going on submission

The distinct differences between YA and Adult fiction

What her screenwriting background taught her about fast-paced storytelling

Why fanfiction provides writers an early anonymous feedback loop

And a lot more!
